To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the soil N availability to maize in Tanzanian highlands was affected by fertilizer application, and the soil type, and this was reflected in the yield.

1) soil inorganic N was depleted in the first N application and was exposed to the risk of leaching; 2) the second N application was the main contributor to maize yield; and 3) soil type was the main contributor of the yield difference.
the N availability to maize is affected by soil type and N application rate in the Tanzanian Highlands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of soil type and fertilizer application on nitrogen availability to maize in Tanzania, a country in Sub Saharan Africa.
the effect of soil and fertilizer management on nitrogen availability to maize in Tanzania.

the following: (1) to assess the effect of soil type and fertilizer application rate on the availability of inorganic nitrogen (N) in the soil and on the yield of maize, (2) to determine the relationship between the amount of N in the soil and maize yield, and (3) to identify the most appropriate rate of urea application for maize in the two different soil types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N fertilizer application rate should be adjusted to the soil type to ensure the proper N supply for maize production in the Tanzanian Highlands.
soil type is the major contributor to N availability to maize in Tanzania, and that N application rates and timing are important to maximize N availability in the Tanzanian Highlands.

the application of N fertilizer at a rate of 150 kg ha 1 (split into two dressings at 75 kg ha 1 each) was sufficient to meet the crop N demand in TZm, while in TZi a higher rate of 150 150 kg N fertilizer ha 1 was needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N fertilizer application should be adjusted according to the N demand of the crop, and to the soil type to ensure a sufficient supply of N to the crop.
in the Tanzanian Highlands, soil inorganic N was more efficiently maintained at the tasselling stage in the clayey Andisolic soil than in the sandy Alfisols.
N fertilizer application in the second N supply (major N application) could be more efficient in increasing maize N uptake and yield in the Tanzanian Andisols than in sandy Alfisols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N fertilizer rate should be increased with increasing soil N retention capacity to ensure the synchrony between crop N demand and soil N availability.
the timing of N application and soil N availability should be carefully considered to maximize the yield of maize in different agro-ecological zones in SSA.
inorganic N availability to the crop is a key factor for maize yield and that the soil type plays a major role on N availability and thus crop yield.
